title: Post-Survey
description: 感谢您完成 case 审核。请回答以下关于您对 AI 起草工具的整体看法。约 6–8 分钟。

items.text: I trust the AI drafts to be clinically reasonable starting points.
I would feel comfortable sending an AI draft after only a quick review.
The AI draft tool generally captures the most important issues.
It was clear what information the AI used when drafting the reply.
I could tell when the AI was uncertain or relying on weak evidence.
I could tell when the AI's reasoning did not match the chart.
Reviewing AI drafts in this format would fit into my normal workflow.
Reviewing AI drafts saved me effort compared to writing replies from scratch.
The interface added cognitive burden to my decision-making.
I, as the reviewing clinician, am ultimately responsible for what gets sent to the patient.
If the AI draft contained an error and I sent it as is, I would be primarily responsible.
Clear responsibility boundaries between clinician and AI tool exist in this workflow.
I worry that clinicians might rely on AI drafts more than they should.
I worry that I personally might rely on AI drafts more than I should.
Time pressure could make clinicians send AI drafts without sufficient review.
What feature, if added, would most improve your ability to review AI drafts safely?
Any other comments about the experience?
